# SK0280 — The base list names an interface it already has

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A base list naming an interface that another entry in the same list already brings in.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Cleanup |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

`class Buffer : IList<byte>, IEnumerable<byte>` says the same thing twice, and the second saying is the expensive one: a reader who knows `IList<T>` extends `IEnumerable<T>` has to stop and work out whether the author knew it too, or whether the second entry is there because something about this type is different. Nothing about it is. ⚠ The shape belongs disproportionately to generated code, because a model that has been asked for "a list that can be enumerated" writes down both nouns it was given.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
interface IReader {
    int Read();
}

interface ISeekableReader : IReader {
    void Seek(int offset);
}

sealed class FileReader : ISeekableReader, IReader {
    public int Read() => 0;

    public void Seek(int offset) { }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
sealed class FileReader : ISeekableReader {
    public int Read() => 0;

    public void Seek(int offset) { }
}
```

## The ReSharper mapping

⚠ **Narrower than ReSharper's inspection, and the difference is a correctness argument rather than a scope cut.** `RedundantExtendsListEntry` reports two shapes and `jb inspectcode` 2025.2.6 was run on both: an interface implied by another *interface* in the same list (`class C : IDerived, IBase`), and an interface implied by the *base class* (`class D : B, IBase` where `B : IBase`). Skala ships only the first. Re-listing an interface on a derived class makes that class re-implement it, so the interface mapping is recomputed there — a member declared `new` in the derived class becomes the implementation instead of the base's, and deleting the entry silently changes which method an interface call reaches.

⚠ **Nothing in the SDK hosts either shape, and the zero was measured.** Reading `IsEnabledByDefault`/`DefaultSeverity` out of SDK 10.0.400's analyzer assemblies gives 442 descriptors and none of them is this; a probe with all 120 `IDE` ids and all 320 `CA` ids forced to `warning`, `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild=true`, `AnalysisMode=All` and `AnalysisLevel=latest-all` reported nothing on `class C : IDerived, IBase`, on a compilation where `IDE0055`, `IDE0160`, `IDE0380` and `CA1051` all fired and there was no `AD0001`.

⚠ `class C : object` is **not** this finding. ReSharper does not report it either — probed in the same run.

## When it does not fire

⚠ **An interface implied by the *base class* is never reported**, only one implied by another interface written in the same list. Re-listing an interface on a derived type re-implements it there, so the interface mapping is recomputed in the derived type and a `new` member becomes the implementation — dropping the entry would change which method an interface call reaches. Where one interface entry implies another there is no such hazard: the type has to implement the derived interface either way, so the mapping is computed in the same place with or without the redundant name. ⚠ **A default interface member anywhere in the closure withdraws the finding.** Where an interface declares a member with a body, or re-abstracts one it inherited, the written interface set is part of deciding which implementation is most specific, and that is a question about method resolution rather than about duplication. ⚠ **A `[ComImport]` type is never reported**: the declared interface order is the vtable layout, so an entry that is redundant to C# is load-bearing to the marshaller. ⚠ **Explicit implementation does *not* withdraw it, and that is the shape most likely to be got wrong.** `void IBase.A()` needs `IBase` in the type's interface set, which it still is through the derived interface, so the code compiles and means the same thing; there is a fixture asserting it. ⚠ One entry is reported per declaration per pass: two deletions on one base list have disjoint spans but not independent commas, and the next pass over the fixed text sees the rest.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK0280.severity`
